captions.instagram:
How does a harmonium work?

Every note on a harmonium is a thin brass tongue buzzing through a slot, fed by air you pump with one hand. Take one apart in 3D, scrape a reed to tune it, pull the stops, hear why its fixed notes got it banned from All India Radio, and play it with your keyboard.

→ A harmonium is a wooden box of brass reeds, a keyboard and a bellows you pump by hand.
→ Pump, and air waits under pressure. Press a key, and it rushes out through brass reeds.
→ Each note is a brass tongue riveted over a slot. Air pushes it through, and it springs back.
→ A shorter tongue swings faster: halve its length and the note climbs two octaves.
→ Each push of the bellows fills a spring-loaded reservoir, which keeps the wind steady.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/harmoniumclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does a harmonium work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Every note on a harmonium is a thin brass tongue buzzing through a slot, fed by air you pump with one hand. Take one apart in 3D, scrape a reed to tune it, pull the stops, hear why its fixed notes got it banned from All India Radio, and play it with your keyboard.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/harmoniumclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/harmoniumclear

In this video:
• A box of reeds and a bellows. An Indian harmonium is a wooden box with a keyboard on top and a hinged bellows at the back.
• A brass tongue that chops the air. Each note is a free reed: a thin brass tongue riveted over a slot.
• Pump, store, squeeze. Your hand pushes air through a one-way valve into a reservoir held shut by springs.
• Pull a stop, add a voice. Each stop opens a bank of reeds: bass an octave down, male at the key's pitch, female an octave up.
• Fixed notes in a sliding music. The reeds are tuned once, usually to equal temperament: Ga is 400 cents above Sa, while the pure 5/4 Ga that singers lean to is 386.
• From church organ to every stage in India. Missionaries brought pedal reed organs; in Calcutta, Dwarkanath Ghose is widely credited with the hand-pumped floor harmonium by 1875.
